comparison: First preserved full-video run versus final rerun after CLI boundary fixes
comparison_rule: pandas assert_frame_equal(check_dtype=False,check_exact=True): identical shapes, columns, status/Boolean values, numeric values and missing-value locations; no rounding tolerance.
revision_scope: Only analyze_motion_v2.py changed among the five inference source hashes retained in all video summaries. Fusion, frontend, legacy signal processing and basic POS/CHROM source hashes remained unchanged.
CLI normalizes empty numerical HR columns to float before reference scoring, allowing shorter-than-window video to produce an empty score table without crashing.
At a nominal 6-second minimum and fractional fps, CLI rounds frame count upward if nearest rounding would yield less than 6 seconds; requested_window_s is recorded.
All five assessed videos request 10-second windows, and their effective frame windows and nominal +/-5-second device-HR reference convention are unchanged.
The first freeze precedes the first reference scoring. The final protocol file is a rerun snapshot, not a claim that no real-reference results had yet been seen.

The evaluator previously received a documented numerical-SNR-sign audit fix (1e-9 dB equality tolerance) before both evaluation_initial and evaluation used here; its hash is unchanged between these two evaluations.
notes: This audit establishes that the CLI revision leaves these five 10-second-window results unchanged; it does not establish behavior on all other inputs.

No original CLI source snapshot was reconstructed for a textual source diff; changed-file identification uses preserved source hashes, and the boundary behavior is documented in the current code and CLI regression tests.
